key_insight: AegisDx reframes AI diagnosis as a safety-first reasoning workflow that explicitly looks for dangerous missed diagnoses, verifies evidence, and structures next steps instead of making a single prediction.
clinical_relevance: In acute care, this kind of framework may help clinicians see broader differentials and reduce the chance of overlooking high-risk conditions.
method: Coordinates multiple LLM roles with contracts and structured intermediate outputs
Uses evidence retrieval and verification gates to check reasoning against grounded medical sources
Forces explicit screening for “must-not-miss” conditions and actionable follow-up steps
evidence_signal: Across literature cases and emergency department notes, AegisDx outperformed standalone LLM baselines on top-3 accuracy and improved physician-rated safety, including must-not-miss detection.
watch_item: Performance gains were shown in evaluation settings, so real-world reliability, workflow integration, and oversight requirements still need careful validation before clinical use.
paper_title: A safety-oriented hypothetico-deductive framework for AI-assisted differential diagnosis
